# Water system numbers (generated by sim/water/water.py)

Status: tested in simulation. Pump values: datasheets or shop pages (see `PUMPS` in the script). Not measured.
Geometry (F3 trolley): nozzle 0.905 m over the floor. Lift -0.90 m (full bag) to -0.62 m (empty bag): the water surface is above the nozzle. 3.3 m of 3.2 mm tube, 2 L bag. Ranges: from the nozzle to the floor.

Equivalent constant drag for `aim/` (`ControllerConfig.drag`): 0.110 1/m (fit to the best estimate at +15°).
Jet speed against the pack voltage: v0 = 9.6 m/s × (V / 22.2 V)^0.79 (fit from 21 V and 25.2 V, ASSUMED speed ~ voltage).

## Water held when the pump is off

The water surface is up to 1.80 m high. It pushes water through the stopped pump toward the nozzle.
- Robot standing, nozzle tilted down (0.855 m): 9.3 kPa.
- Robot on the floor (nozzle 0.10 m): 16.6 kPa.
- The check valves in series open at 20 kPa. They hold the water in both cases.

## Fire capacity (recommended pump and nozzle)

- Water flow 6.7 g/s. If all of it evaporates, it takes 18 kW. This is an upper limit: on a real fire much of the water runs off.
- At the hand-application rates of 9 to 15 L/(m2 min), the flow covers 269 to 449 cm2 of fire floor area, a square of 16 to 21 cm.
- A loose paper fire of that area peaks at about 8 to 22 kW.
